The Central Bank of Nigeria has begun engaging with Nigerian and Chinese businesses to address cross-border payment challenges, strengthen banking relationships, and improve financial flows between the two countries. The initiative aims to identify obstacles affecting transactions between businesses in both economies and explore measures to improve access to financial services, investment opportunities, and remittance channels. This was disclosed in a statement issued by the apex bank on Thursday following a high-level business and financial roundtable held in Beijing, China, on Wednesday, October 21, 2026. The CBN said, “Issues raised included the need for more efficient cross-border payment arrangements, stronger banking connectivity, and the potential benefits of a larger Nigerian banking presence in China.” According to the statement, the meeting took place at the Pan Pacific Beijing and brought together business leaders and financial stakeholders from both countries. The engagement provided an opportunity for businesses operating across the two markets to share their experiences and identify practical challenges affecting financial transactions and investment flows. He explained that insights from such discussions would help the apex bank identify opportunities to develop deeper and more accessible financial markets. The Deputy Governor for Economic Policy, Philip Ikeazor, delivered the opening remarks, highlighting the need to translate improvements in Nigeria’s macroeconomic fundamentals into increased investment and stronger financial markets. Nigeria’s Ambassador to China, Lt. Gen. Abdulrahman Dambazau (retd.), also addressed participants. The statement explained that an interactive listening session formed a central part of the engagement, allowing participants to discuss transaction difficulties and opportunities for improving financial connectivity. Discussions also examined the potential benefits of expanding the presence of Nigerian banks in China to support businesses conducting transactions between both countries. Participants were further briefed on Nigeria’s economic reforms, improving macroeconomic conditions and emerging investment opportunities in its financial markets. In his closing remarks, Cardoso stressed the importance of using feedback from businesses to identify financial and institutional challenges requiring attention. The apex bank said, “The insights gathered are expected to inform the CBN’s continued engagement with relevant financial institutions and regulatory counterparts, focusing on practical areas for cooperation within the Bank’s mandate.” The Beijing meeting forms part of the CBN’s broader strategy to strengthen Nigeria’s financial relationships across Asia, following earlier engagements in Singapore and at the IMF and World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok. The bank said its China programme also includes bilateral discussions with the People’s Bank of China, engagements with the leadership of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, and meetings with Nigerian and Chinese businesses. The programme will extend to Guangzhou, where the CBN plans to hold another listening session with the Nigerian business community. According to the bank, the Guangzhou engagement will focus on understanding the financial challenges facing Nigerian businesses, strengthening remittance channels, and exploring opportunities to facilitate investment in Nigeria.
